_about: Hand-picked documentary topics (written once, offline). Each is a true, widely documented story with its own English Wikipedia article and many independent sources, so research can verify it. Research still checks every fact; nothing here is ever narrated unverified.

topics.title: The Wave of Syrup That Flooded Boston
topics.question: How did a flood of molasses kill people in a city street?
topics.hook: A wave of syrup flattened a Boston street.
topics.payoff: A badly built, overfilled storage tank burst and released millions of gallons of molasses at once.
topics.why_visual: A giant brown wave rolling through tiny cartoon streets and trains.
visual_metaphors: a cracked tank leaking like a juice box
people stuck like flies on flypaper

topics.title: The Summer When People Danced Until They Collapsed
topics.question: Why did hundreds of people in Strasbourg dance for weeks?
topics.hook: One woman started dancing. Then she couldn't stop.
topics.payoff: Historians link it to mass psychogenic illness in a town crushed by famine and disease.
topics.why_visual: A packed medieval square of dancers, musicians hired to keep them going.
visual_metaphors: dancers like wind-up toys
a town council scratching its head

topics.title: The Explosion That Flattened a City Before the Bomb
topics.question: How did one ship collision destroy half of Halifax?
topics.hook: Two ships bumped. A city disappeared.
topics.payoff: A French ship packed with wartime explosives caught fire after the collision and detonated in the harbour.
topics.category: forgotten stories that changed the world
topics.why_visual: Two small ships nudging, then a giant white mushroom over a harbour town.
visual_metaphors: ships as bumper cars
a city map torn in half

topics.title: The Blast That Flattened a Forest With No Crater
topics.question: What knocked down millions of trees in Siberia without leaving a hole?
topics.hook: Eighty million trees fell. Nothing hit the ground.
topics.payoff: A space rock most likely exploded in the air several kilometres up, so the shockwave did the damage.
topics.why_visual: A forest of matchsticks lying flat in a giant butterfly pattern.
visual_metaphors: trees as dominoes
a fireball popping like a balloon

topics.title: The Year Summer Never Came
topics.question: Why did it snow in June across Europe and America in 1816?
topics.hook: It snowed in June. Crops died everywhere.
topics.payoff: The huge eruption of Mount Tambora a year earlier filled the sky with ash and cooled the planet.
topics.why_visual: Snow on summer fields, a volcano far away puffing a grey blanket around the globe.
visual_metaphors: a sun wearing sunglasses of ash
farmers in coats holding dead corn

topics.title: The Glowing Paint That Poisoned Its Painters
topics.question: Why were factory girls told to lick radium-paint brushes?
topics.hook: They were told to lick the glowing brushes.
topics.payoff: Radium built up in their bones; their court fight changed worker safety law.
topics.category: forgotten stories that changed the world
topics.why_visual: Rows of workers painting glowing watch dials in a dark factory.
visual_metaphors: green glow spreading like a stain
a judge's gavel lighting up

topics.title: The Smell That Forced London to Rebuild
topics.question: How did one hot summer give London its sewers?
topics.hook: Parliament could not breathe inside its own building.
topics.payoff: The stench of the Thames in 1858 finally pushed Parliament to fund Joseph Bazalgette's sewer network.
topics.why_visual: Politicians with clothespins on noses, a brown river, then giant brick tunnels.
visual_metaphors: stink lines as cartoon ghosts
curtains soaked in lime

topics.title: When One Flower Bulb Cost a House
topics.question: Did tulips really become more expensive than houses?
topics.hook: A single flower bulb cost a house.
topics.payoff: Prices for rare bulbs in 1630s Holland spiked on futures contracts and then collapsed in 1637.
topics.why_visual: Traders in a tavern bidding on a striped tulip, a price chart shooting up then crashing.
visual_metaphors: a tulip on a golden throne
a chart like a rollercoaster

topics.title: The Soda Company That Changed Its Recipe and Panicked
topics.question: Why did Coca-Cola bring back the old formula in 79 days?
topics.hook: Coca-Cola changed its taste. America revolted.
topics.payoff: Blind tests liked the new taste, but fans felt their old Coke was taken away, so Coca-Cola Classic returned.
topics.category: weird business decisions and their consequences
topics.why_visual: Protest signs, hotline phones ringing, a can swapped back on a shelf.
visual_metaphors: a can wearing a disguise
a phone melting from calls

topics.title: The Bridge That Danced Itself Apart
topics.question: How did gentle wind destroy a brand-new steel bridge?
topics.hook: A gentle wind tore a steel bridge apart.
topics.payoff: Wind made the thin, flexible deck twist in a self-feeding flutter until it broke.
topics.why_visual: A bridge waving like a ribbon, a car abandoned in the middle.
visual_metaphors: the bridge as a jump rope
engineers holding rulers that bend

topics.title: The Fake Skull That Fooled Science for Forty Years
topics.question: How did a forged fossil fool experts for decades?
topics.hook: The missing link was a painted fake.
topics.payoff: In 1953 tests showed a human skull and an orangutan jaw stained to look ancient.
topics.why_visual: Scientists in a gravel pit, a skull and jaw that don't match, a fluorine test tube.
visual_metaphors: a jaw with a fake moustache
a museum label peeling off

topics.title: The War Named After a Sailor's Ear
topics.question: How did one cut-off ear start a war?
topics.hook: A captain carried his own ear to Parliament.
topics.payoff: Robert Jenkins' story became fuel for Britain's trade quarrel with Spain, which turned into open war in 1739.
topics.why_visual: A sailor holding up a jar, politicians gasping, ships firing.
visual_metaphors: an ear in a jar like a pickle
a map split by a sword

topics.title: The Pig That Almost Started a War
topics.question: How did one shot pig bring two empires to the brink?
topics.hook: A farmer shot a pig. Two empires mobilised.
topics.payoff: The 1859 standoff on San Juan Island ended without a battle, and the only casualty was the pig.
topics.why_visual: A pig in a potato patch, soldiers and warships facing off on a tiny island.
visual_metaphors: the pig on a war map
cannons pointing at a potato

topics.title: The Ship Found Sailing With Nobody Aboard
topics.question: What happened to the crew of the Mary Celeste?
topics.hook: The ship was fine. Everyone was gone.
topics.payoff: Nobody knows for sure; the leading idea is that the crew fled in the lifeboat fearing a problem, and was lost.
topics.category: events that seemed impossible but have a factual explanation
topics.why_visual: An empty ship drifting, sailors from another ship climbing aboard.
visual_metaphors: a ghostly outline at the wheel
a lifeboat-shaped gap

topics.title: The Man Who Survived an Iron Rod Through His Head
topics.question: How did Phineas Gage live after a rod went through his skull?
topics.hook: An iron rod flew through his skull. He talked.
topics.payoff: The rod missed vital areas; his changed behaviour helped science link brain regions to personality.
topics.why_visual: A railway worker, a rod shooting upward, a doctor's notebook.
visual_metaphors: the rod as a giant arrow
a brain map lighting up

topics.title: The Mightiest Warship That Sank on Its First Trip
topics.question: Why did Sweden's mightiest warship sink on its maiden voyage?
topics.hook: The mightiest warship set sail. Then it sank.
topics.payoff: The Vasa was too top-heavy for its narrow hull, and a gust of wind tipped it over.
topics.why_visual: A gilded ship leaving harbour, tilting, crowds on shore.
visual_metaphors: the ship as a tall wobbly cake
a king's crown falling in water

topics.title: The Space Probe Lost to a Units Mix-Up
topics.question: How did a missing unit conversion destroy a Mars probe?
topics.hook: A Mars probe died from a math mistake.
topics.payoff: One team's software used imperial units while another expected metric, so the orbiter flew too low into Mars.
topics.why_visual: Two offices with different rulers, a probe skimming too close to a red planet.
visual_metaphors: a ruler in feet fighting a ruler in metres
the probe as a paper plane

topics.title: The Jet That Ran Out of Fuel Over Canada and Landed Anyway
topics.question: How did an airliner with empty tanks land safely?
topics.hook: The airliner ran out of fuel. Everyone survived.
topics.payoff: A fuel calculation mixed up pounds and kilograms; the pilots glided to a former airbase at Gimli.
topics.why_visual: A silent jet gliding over fields, a drag strip with racing cars below.
visual_metaphors: the jet as a paper glider
a fuel gauge with an empty sad face

topics.title: The Giant Airship That Burned in Seconds
topics.question: What destroyed the Hindenburg so fast?
topics.hook: The giant airship burned in seconds.
topics.payoff: Its hydrogen caught fire, most likely from a static spark near leaking gas, as it landed in New Jersey.
topics.why_visual: A huge silver airship over a mooring mast, then fire racing along it.
visual_metaphors: the airship as a cigar
a spark like a tiny firefly

topics.title: The Toads Sent to Eat Beetles That Ate Australia Instead
topics.question: How did a pest-control plan become Australia's pest?
topics.hook: They brought toads to save sugar cane.
topics.payoff: The cane toads ignored the beetles, multiplied fast, and spread across northern Australia, poisoning predators.
topics.why_visual: A crate of toads becoming a carpet of toads across a map.
visual_metaphors: toads as a marching army
a beetle laughing on a cane stalk

topics.title: The War on Sparrows That Brought Locusts
topics.question: How did killing sparrows lead to a famine of crops?
topics.hook: A country declared war on sparrows.
topics.payoff: With the sparrows gone, insects like locusts boomed and ate the crops, worsening the Great Chinese Famine.
topics.category: forgotten stories that changed the world
topics.why_visual: Crowds banging pots to keep birds flying, then clouds of insects.
visual_metaphors: exhausted birds dropping from the sky
locusts in tiny bibs

topics.title: The Mould That Grew on a Forgotten Dish
topics.question: How did a messy lab bench give the world antibiotics?
topics.hook: He came back from holiday to a mouldy dish.
topics.payoff: Alexander Fleming noticed the mould killed bacteria around it: penicillin.
topics.why_visual: A cluttered lab, a petri dish with a clean ring around fuzzy mould.
visual_metaphors: bacteria running from the mould
a dish wearing a superhero cape

topics.title: The Walk in the Woods That Invented Velcro
topics.question: How did burrs on a dog become a fastener?
topics.hook: His dog came home covered in burrs.
topics.payoff: George de Mestral studied the burrs' tiny hooks and copied them into hook-and-loop fastener.
topics.why_visual: A dog in a field, a microscope showing hooks, a shoe strap closing.
visual_metaphors: burrs as tiny grappling hooks
a dog annoyed in a burr coat

topics.title: The Chocolate Bar That Melted in a Radar Lab
topics.question: How did radar research lead to the microwave oven?
topics.hook: A chocolate bar melted in his pocket.
topics.payoff: Engineer Percy Spencer realised the radar magnetron's microwaves heated food, and Raytheon built the first microwave oven.
topics.why_visual: A lab of glowing tubes, a gooey pocket, popcorn exploding.
visual_metaphors: the chocolate bar sweating
popcorn as fireworks

topics.title: The Officials Thrown Out of a Castle Window
topics.question: Why did throwing men from a window start a thirty-year war?
topics.hook: They threw the officials out the window.
topics.payoff: The 1618 Defenestration of Prague sparked the revolt that grew into the Thirty Years' War; the men survived the fall.
topics.why_visual: A castle window, men falling into a dung heap, armies gathering.
visual_metaphors: officials as tossed laundry
a map of Europe catching fire

topics.title: The Beer Tsunami That Hit a London Street
topics.question: How did beer flood a London neighbourhood?
topics.hook: A wave of beer swept through London.
topics.payoff: A huge vat at the Meux brewery burst in 1814 and knocked over others, releasing a flood of beer.
topics.why_visual: Giant wooden vats, a foamy wave crashing through brick houses.
visual_metaphors: a hoop popping off a barrel
foam like snow drifts

topics.title: The Tower That Started Leaning Before It Was Finished
topics.question: Why does the Tower of Pisa lean, and why hasn't it fallen?
topics.hook: It started leaning before it was finished.
topics.payoff: Its foundation sits on soft soil; builders compensated for centuries, and modern engineers stabilised it by removing soil.
topics.search: Leaning Tower of Pisa soil stabilisation
topics.why_visual: A white tower tilting floor by floor, engineers pulling soil out.
visual_metaphors: the tower as a stack of plates
a giant tilting at a café table

topics.title: The Iceman Who Was Murdered 5,000 Years Ago
topics.question: How did hikers find a 5,000-year-old murder victim?
topics.hook: Hikers found a body. It was 5,300 years old.
topics.payoff: Ötzi was preserved in Alpine ice, and scans later found an arrowhead in his shoulder.
topics.category: events that seemed impossible but have a factual explanation
topics.why_visual: Hikers on a glacier, a scanner revealing an arrowhead.
visual_metaphors: the iceman in a freezer of time
an X-ray with a tiny arrow

topics.title: The Ancient Computer Pulled From a Shipwreck
topics.question: What was a bronze gear machine doing in a 2,000-year-old wreck?
topics.hook: Divers found a computer older than Rome's emperors.
topics.payoff: The Antikythera mechanism was a hand-cranked Greek device that predicted eclipses and planet positions.
topics.why_visual: Sponge divers, a corroded lump, glowing gears and a sky map.
visual_metaphors: gears like a clock's skeleton
planets on strings

topics.title: The Dead Man Who Fooled Hitler's Spies
topics.question: How did a corpse with fake papers change the invasion of Sicily?
topics.hook: A dead man carried the war's biggest lie.
topics.payoff: British intelligence planted fake invasion plans on a body, and Germany moved forces away from Sicily.
topics.why_visual: A briefcase chained to a body, spies reading letters, troops moving the wrong way.
visual_metaphors: a map with a giant fake arrow
spies with magnifying glasses

topics.title: The Army Made of Inflatable Tanks
topics.question: How did artists with balloons fool an army?
topics.hook: Two men lifted a tank over their heads.
topics.payoff: The Ghost Army used inflatable tanks, sound trucks and fake radio traffic to mislead German forces.
topics.why_visual: Soldiers carrying a rubber tank, speakers blasting fake engine noise.
visual_metaphors: a tank deflating with a squeak
a pump labelled 'army'

topics.title: The Town That Blew Up a Whale
topics.question: Why did Oregon use dynamite to remove a dead whale?
topics.hook: They used dynamite to move a dead whale.
topics.payoff: Engineers expected the blast to blow it to tiny pieces for gulls; instead chunks rained on the crowd and a car.
topics.why_visual: A beach crowd, a big boom, blubber falling like rain, a squashed car.
visual_metaphors: seagulls with napkins
a car roof with a dent

topics.title: The Plot to Blow Up Parliament With Hidden Barrels
topics.question: How was the Gunpowder Plot discovered hours before the blast?
topics.hook: Thirty-six barrels sat under Parliament.
topics.payoff: An anonymous warning letter led a search that found Guy Fawkes guarding the gunpowder.
topics.why_visual: A dark cellar of barrels, a lantern, a letter changing hands.
visual_metaphors: barrels hiding under a rug
a letter as a paper bird

topics.title: The Fire That Started in a Bakery and Took London
topics.question: How did one bakery fire burn most of the City of London?
topics.hook: A bakery fire burned down a city.
topics.payoff: Dry timber houses, strong wind and slow decisions let the 1666 fire spread for four days.
topics.category: forgotten stories that changed the world
topics.search: Great Fire of London 1666 Pudding Lane
topics.why_visual: A tiny oven spark, wooden streets, flames jumping rooftops, St Paul's dome.
visual_metaphors: flames as running cartoon figures
a mayor shrugging

topics.title: The Moon Mission Saved by Duct Tape
topics.question: How did Apollo 13's crew get home after an explosion?
topics.hook: Their oxygen tank exploded halfway to the Moon.
topics.payoff: The crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat and a taped-together air filter until they swung around the Moon and home.
topics.search: Apollo 13 lunar module lifeboat CO2 filter
topics.why_visual: A spacecraft venting gas, astronauts in a cramped module, a square filter in a round hole.
visual_metaphors: a square peg in a round hole
the Moon as a giant slingshot

topics.title: The Investment Craze That Made a Company Worth More Than a Country
topics.question: How did the South Sea Company's shares soar and crash in one year?
topics.hook: Isaac Newton lost a fortune on one stock.
topics.payoff: Hype and insider deals pushed South Sea shares up in 1720 until they collapsed, ruining many investors.
topics.why_visual: A coffee house of shouting traders, a soap bubble with a ship inside, then pop.
visual_metaphors: share certificates as paper planes
a bubble with a price tag

topics.title: The Missile That Destroyed Itself Over a Number
topics.question: How did one software number make a rocket self-destruct?
topics.hook: A rocket destroyed itself over one number.
topics.payoff: Ariane 5 reused old code where a value overflowed, so guidance failed and the rocket self-destructed in 1996.
topics.why_visual: A rocket lifting off, a tiny number too big for its box, a puff of smoke.
visual_metaphors: a number squeezing into a tiny box
the rocket doing a confused U-turn

topics.title: The Meat That Fell From a Clear Sky
topics.question: What made chunks of meat rain down on Kentucky in 1876?
topics.hook: It rained meat in Kentucky.
topics.payoff: The leading explanation is that vultures threw up their food while flying overhead.
topics.category: events that seemed impossible but have a factual explanation
topics.why_visual: A farmyard, a sunny sky, flakes of red falling, vultures far above.
visual_metaphors: a vulture looking guilty
a farmer holding an umbrella against meat

topics.title: The Town Whose Ground Has Burned Since 1962
topics.question: Why has a Pennsylvania town's coal mine been burning since 1962?
topics.hook: This town's ground has burned since 1962.
topics.payoff: A fire spread into the coal seams under Centralia, and it has smouldered underground ever since, emptying the town.
topics.why_visual: Smoke rising through cracked roads, empty houses, a map of glowing tunnels.
visual_metaphors: the town on a stove
a road with a steam vent like a kettle
